newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crudes rise after Alaska crude sale.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crudes rise after Alaska crude sale.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices edged up Tuesday after a cargo of Alaskan crude was sold at a slightly smaller discount, traders said.
The shrinking discount for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude, which has tightened eight cents a barrel since June, stood at $2.04 under September West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude.
Traders said Exxon sold to a large, New York-based oil company with refiners along the West Coast.
Another large West Coast refiner was rumored to have bought a cargo of ANS at $2.07 under from Exxon last week, traders said.
Kern River and Wilmington grades rose after major oil companies raised prices late Monday.
